pr_title: Avoid accounting for the pause pitch adjust effect when "fixing" hardware offset adjustments
pr_body:
Bit of an unfortunate one. Because we are applying the pitch adjustment to the lowest level (`Track`), it's hard to filter out in parent clock calculations.

Tried a few solutions but this feels the best. Note that we can't just undo the `pauseFreqAdjust` adjustment as it will div-by-zero.

Closes https://github.com/ppy/osu/issues/14773.
pr_comments:
I'm going to block temporarily as there is some cross-over in what this is fixing and https://github.com/ppy/osu/pull/14361, which looks to be addressing an issue with a similar cause. Potentially a combined or similar solution can be implemented there as well.

Would still appreciate feedback on the direction of this PR
I 100% agree with this one over the other linked alternative because I could actually understand what this is doing in 15 minutes.

Tentatively unblocking this one as I'm not really ready to make any calls on the other PR. On a second read I don't think this PR adds too much new complexity and fixes a majority failure case, but I'm also fine with leaving it for now if anyone disagrees.

issue_context.title: You can rewind a map while in the middle of playing (caused by offset being applied every time a map is paused)
issue_context.body:
Extension of discovery from #14770, though not strictly related. Credit to zachmanthethird

**When playing with an Audio offset, upon resuming from pause, the offset is stacked again onto the map again (though the mp3 offset remains consistent).** 

If I play with +500 offset, when I pause, upon resuming all objects appear to reset back to their position at 0 offset, effectively "turning back time" by 500ms. This can be done multiple times throughout the map.

Best to watch the videos below to understand.

**Example with osu!catch:** 
beatmap used: https://osu.ppy.sh/beatmapsets/393995#fruits/857602
https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/30021847/133720702-9205ec00-c0e0-41b4-9531-9d384c99adc6.mp4

**Further example with osu!taiko:**
beatmap used: https://osu.ppy.sh/beatmapsets/958476#taiko/2006816
https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/30021847/133720736-8ff6b034-e89a-4030-b300-1e9a7f37bec9.mp4

**Interesting behaviour with finishers having their combo counted twice when reverted. This ONLY happens to finishers when hit with both sides of the drum:**
beatmap used: https://osu.ppy.sh/beatmapsets/566725#taiko/1200449
https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/30021847/133720768-1d6fcc5f-8251-4147-b120-c0911de7d51b.mp4

This bug works in reverse too. So playing with -500 offset will skip the map forward in time by 500ms each time you pause (considerably less abuseable since it only leads to misses).

In additon, the bugged scores also submit for osu!
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/30021847/133719983-cb76e8a7-06d5-4b08-b2e6-382539826f8b.png)

Using the osu!plus extension also shows that the score submitted with 47/40x combo which obviously is not intended.
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/30021847/133720081-3ff6d718-e475-4a63-81a6-00b7c610ef0b.png)

**osu!lazer version: 2021.916.0**

comments: Sounds like the wrong clock is being seeked in the forced-seek we perform on resuming gameplay.

review_comments:
The only case I'm afraid of with this way is if `CurrentTime` gets accessed before the first call to `ProcessFrame`, where seeking to a certain position would apply the offset inversely in `MasterGameplayClockContainer.Seek()` but would still not have `CurrentTime` correct due to `offsetAdjust` still being zero.

That should theortically be the case in `MultiSpectatorScreen`, as it stops the clock before the first `Update` call to the gameplay clock container where the clock would receive the first `ProcessFrame` (and even if it gets it somehow, it will still be blocked by `pauseRateAdjust.Value` already being not one):
https://github.com/ppy/osu/blob/9bacc0d50cae548b89341e14507c0c9e54189966/osu.Game/Screens/OnlinePlay/Multiplayer/Spectate/MultiSpectatorScreen.cs#L150-L159

Changing `Seek` so that it also has this `offsetAdjust` logic might be one way to solve this, however.

Not forgotten, but I'm also not sure if valid.. I'll need to read this comment multiple more times to understand the implications. Having a test scene covering the issue/regression would definitely be helpful.
I didn't forget about this review comment. I just don't understand what it's trying to say or what a practical scenario for reproducing such a failure would be.
